title: Microbial cfDNA Sample Processing and Extraction Protocol
author: Martin Schou Pedersen

steps.title: Initial Sample Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Streck Cell-Free DNA BCT sample tubes at 1,600 × g (RCF) for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Plasma Isolation and Clarification
steps.instruction: Isolate plasma and remove cellular debris via high-speed centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Pipette plasma into 2 mL LoBind tubes, ensuring a maximum of 1 mL per tube to avoid suboptimal pelleting of cells.
Centrifuge at 15,595 × g (RCF) for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge tubes at 200 × g for 30 seconds to collect liquid from the cap.

steps.title: Plasma Allocation and Storage
steps.instruction: Allocate the required plasma for extraction and store the remainder.

substeps.instruction: Allocate 3 mL plasma per sample for extraction.
Pipette residual plasma (expected total volume 4–6 mL per Streck tube) into 2 mL LoBind tubes and store in −80°C freezer.

steps.title: Bead-Based DNA Binding
steps.instruction: Prepare the binding reaction and incubate the samples.

substeps.instruction: For each sample, prepare 2 LoBind tubes containing: 1.5 mL Bead Binding Buffer, 45 µL Plasma, 82 µL Magnetic Bead Suspension, and 225 µL Proteinase K.
Incubate tubes at room temperature (15–25°C) for 10 minutes with continuous mixing (invert/tilt) to prevent beads from settling.

steps.title: Bead Washing and Supernatant Removal
steps.instruction: Separate the beads from the liquid using a magnet and clear the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Place the tube on the magnet for >1 minute until the liquid is clear.
Transfer the supernatant to a new Bead Elution tube.
Turn on the Thermomixer and set to 56°C for later use.

steps.title: Bead Processing and Elution
steps.instruction: Process the beads to release the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Transfer contents to a new Bead Elution tube.
Place on Thermomixer at 300 rpm for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove tube from magnet, add 200 µL Bead Elution Buffer, and mix by inversion.

steps.title: Sample Pooling and Final Clarification
steps.instruction: Combine replicates and perform final magnetic separation.

substeps.instruction: Add the liquid from the second tube for the same patient to the emptied tube on the magnet.
Wait 1 minute until the liquid is clear, then remove the supernatant.
Place one tube per patient on the magnet for >1 minute until liquid is clear and remove supernatant.

steps.title: Column Loading and Initial Wash
steps.instruction: Load the DNA onto a purification column and perform the first wash.

substeps.instruction: Prepare one column per sample with a 2 mL collection tube.
Load the supernatant onto the column and centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 minute.
Transfer the column to a new 2 mL collection tube.
Add 300 µL Buffer ACB to the tube, vortex for 10 seconds, and centrifuge briefly to remove liquid from the cap.

steps.title: Column Drying and Conditioning
steps.instruction: Dry the membrane and condition it for elution.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL nuclease-free water to the center of the column membrane and incubate for 1 minute at room temperature.
Incubate on a Thermomixer at 56°C for 3 minutes with the cap open.
Centrifuge at 15,595 × g for 3 minutes.
Transfer the column to a new 1.5 mL Bead Elution tube.

steps.title: Final Column Wash
steps.instruction: Perform the final wash of the column.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL Buffer ACW2 to the column.
Centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 minute.
Transfer the column to a new 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: DNA Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the cfDNA from the column.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 15,595 × g for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at 15,595 × g for 1 minute again and collect the eluate (~50 µL).
Return the 50 µL eluate to the center of the column membrane and incubate for 1 minute at room temperature.

steps.title: Quantification and Storage
steps.instruction: Measure DNA yield and store the sample.

substeps.instruction: Measure the DNA concentration with Qubit (Expected yield: 15–40 ng total).
Store the cfDNA on ice until ready for library preparation; if not proceeding the same day, store at −80°C.
